verses.1:1: The pronouncement that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
verses.1:2: How long, Lord, will I cry out, and You will not listen? Will I call out to You while being wronged, and You will not save?
verses.1:3: Why have You shown me troubles and hardships to look upon, misery and ungodliness? Judgment has come about opposite me, and the judge takes.
verses.1:4: Therefore law has been shattered, and judgment is not carried through to completion, because an ungodly one oppresses the righteous one; for this reason judgment will go out perverted.
verses.1:5: See, you despisers, and look closely, and marvel at marvelous things and vanish; for I am performing a work in your days that you will certainly not believe if anyone recounts it.
verses.1:6: For look, I am raising up the Chaldeans, the bitter and swift nation, which marches across the breadths of the earth to inherit dwellings not its own.
verses.1:7: It is terrifying and imposing; from itself its judgment will come, and its pronouncement will go out from itself.
verses.1:8: And its horses will leap more than leopards, and are fiercer than the wolves of Arabia; and its horsemen will ride out and will rush from afar, and they will fly like an eagle eager to eat.
verses.1:9: Complete destruction will come upon ungodly ones who resist with their faces opposite, and it will gather captives like sand.
verses.1:10: And it will make sport of kings, and tyrants are its playthings; and it will mock at every stronghold, and it will throw up a mound and capture it.
verses.1:11: Then it will change its spirit, and will pass through and make atonement; this strength belongs to my God.
verses.1:12: Are You not from the beginning, Lord God, my Holy One? And we will certainly not die. Lord, You have appointed it for judgment, and He formed me to reprove its discipline.
verses.1:13: Pure is the eye, so as not to see evil things or look upon hardships of pain; why do You look upon those who despise? Will You remain silent while an ungodly one swallows up the righteous one?
verses.1:14: And will You make human beings like the fish of the sea, and like the creeping things that have no leader?
verses.1:15: He drew up complete destruction with a hook, and dragged him in a casting net, and gathered him in his dragnets. For this reason his heart will be glad and rejoice.
verses.1:16: For this reason he will sacrifice to his dragnet and burn incense to his casting net, because by them he fattened his portion, and his foods are choice.
verses.1:17: Therefore he will cast his casting net, and he will not refrain from continually killing nations.
verses.2:1: I will stand upon my watchpost and climb onto a rock, and I will keep watch to see what He will speak in me, and what I should answer concerning my reproof.
verses.2:2: And the Lord replied to me and said, "Write a vision, and clearly on a tablet, so that the one who reads them may run.
verses.2:3: For a vision is still for an appointed time, and it will rise to the end and not in vain; if he lags behind, wait for him, because he will indeed come and will certainly not delay.
verses.2:4: If he shrinks back, My soul takes no pleasure in him; but the righteous one will live by My faithfulness.
verses.2:5: Now the conceited despiser will accomplish nothing at all—he who enlarged his soul like Hades, and this one, like death, is not satisfied; and he will gather together to himself all the nations, and will take in to himself all the peoples.
verses.2:6: Will not all these take up a proverb against him and a riddle as an account about him? And they will say, 'Woe to the one who multiplies for himself things that are not his own—how long?—and weighs down his collar heavily.
verses.2:7: For suddenly those who bite him will rise up, and those who plot against you will wake up, and you will become plunder for them.
verses.2:8: Because you plundered many nations, all the remaining peoples will plunder, because of the bloodshed of human beings and the acts of ungodliness of land and city and all those who inhabit it.
verses.2:9: Alas for the one who greedily takes evil gain for his house, to set his nest on high, to be snatched away from the hand of evils.
verses.2:10: You devised shame for your house; you finished off many peoples, and your soul has sinned.
verses.2:11: For a stone will call out from a wall, and a beetle from timber will utter these things.
verses.2:12: Woe to the one who builds a city with bloodshed, and prepares a city with injustices.
verses.2:13: Are not these things from the Lord Almighty? And numerous peoples failed in fire, and many nations grew fainthearted.
verses.2:14: For the earth will be filled with knowing the glory of the Lord, as water will cover them.
verses.2:15: Alas for the one who gives his neighbor to drink with turbid overthrow, and makes him drunk, so that he may look upon their caves.
verses.2:16: Drink a fullness of dishonor rather than glory, you too; be shaken in heart and quake! The cup of the right hand of the Lord has come around upon you, and dishonor has been gathered upon your glory.
verses.2:17: For the ungodliness of Lebanon will cover you, and the misery of wild beasts will terrify you, because of the bloodshed of human beings and the acts of ungodliness of land and city and all those who inhabit it.
verses.2:18: What profit is a carved image, that they carved it? He molded it as a cast image, a false illusion, because the one who molded it has trusted in his molded work, to make mute idols.
verses.2:19: Woe to the one who says to the wood, "Wake up, rise up!" and to the stone, "Be lifted up!" And it itself is an illusion; and this is a beaten plate of gold and silver, and there is no spirit at all in it.'
verses.2:20: But the Lord is in His holy temple; let all the earth stand in awe before His presence."
verses.3:1: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, with a song.
verses.3:2: Lord, I have heard the report of You, and I feared; I considered Your works, and I was astounded. In the midst of two living creatures You will be known; when the years draw near, You will be recognized; when the appointed time arrives, You will be revealed; when my soul is troubled, in wrath You will remember mercy.
verses.3:3: God will come from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran, shaded and densely wooded. Interlude. His excellence covered the heavens, and the earth is full of His praise.
verses.3:4: And His radiance will be like light; horns are in His hands, and He established a mighty love of His strength.
verses.3:5: Before His face a word will go, and it will go out into the plains at His feet.
verses.3:6: He stood, and the earth was shaken; He looked on, and nations melted away; the mountains were shattered by force, eternal hills melted at His eternal march.
verses.3:7: Instead of troubles I saw the dwellings of the Ethiopians; the tents of the land of Midian will also be terrified.
verses.3:8: Were You angry at rivers, Lord? Or was Your fury at rivers? Or was Your onslaught at the sea? For You will mount Your horses, and Your riding is salvation.
verses.3:9: Surely You drew Your bow against scepters, says the Lord. Interlude. The earth will be split open with rivers.
verses.3:10: Peoples will see You and be in birth pangs, as You scatter waters of passage; the abyss gave its voice, the height of its appearance.
verses.3:11: The sun was lifted up, and the moon stood in its station; Your shafts will go into light, into the radiance of the lightning of Your weapons.
verses.3:12: In threat You will diminish the earth, and in fury You will bring down nations.
verses.3:13: You went out for the salvation of Your people, to save Your anointed one; You will cast death upon the heads of lawless ones; You raised up bonds up to the neck. Interlude.
verses.3:14: You cut through the heads of rulers in astonishment; they will be shaken in it. They will open wide their bridles like a poor person eating in secret.
verses.3:15: And You drive Your horses into the sea, stirring up much water.
verses.3:16: I kept watch, and my belly was terrified at the sound of the prayer of my lips, and trembling entered into my bones, and beneath me my frame was troubled. I will rest in the day of affliction, so as to go up to the people of my sojourn.
verses.3:17: For a fig tree will not bear fruit, and there will be no produce on the vines; the work of the olive tree will prove false, and the fields will not produce food; sheep have failed from food, and there are no oxen at the mangers.
verses.3:18: Yet I will exult in the Lord; I will rejoice in God my Savior.
verses.3:19: The Lord God is my strength, and He will order my feet to completion; He sets me upon the high places, to triumph in His song.

notes.1:3: The Greek text reads "and the judge takes" (implying bribery), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "and strife arises."
notes.1:5: The Septuagint addresses "you despisers" (reflecting Hebrew bogedim rather than MT baggoyim, "among the nations") and adds "and vanish"; this Greek wording is quoted in Acts 13:41.
notes.1:8: The Greek translates the Hebrew consonants for "evening" (erev) as the proper name "Arabia" (Arav).
notes.1:11: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "be guilty" and "to his god," the Greek reads "make atonement" and "to my God," turning the final clause into a confession of the prophet's God.
notes.1:12: The Greek shifts to the third person ("He formed me to reprove its discipline"), reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew consonants behind MT "O Rock, You have established it for reproof."
notes.2:4: The Septuagint reads "by My faithfulness" (or "by faith in Me") rather than MT "by his faithfulness," and together with the masculine "him" in 2:3 forms the wording cited in Hebrews 10:37-38.
notes.2:6: The Greek renders the rare Hebrew term for heavy pledges/debt as "his collar," referring to a heavy neck-collar.
notes.2:11: The Greek reads "a beetle" (a wood-boring beetle) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "a beam" or "rafter."
notes.2:14: The Greek reads "as water will cover them" (referring to the peoples and nations of 2:13) rather than MT "as the waters cover the sea."
notes.2:15: The Greek translates "their caves" (reading Hebrew me'arot) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "their nakedness."
notes.3:2: The Septuagint reads "in the midst of two living creatures You will be known" (vocalizing the Hebrew consonants as shenayim chayyim rather than MT "in the midst of years revive it"), a famous reading widely discussed in early Christian interpretation.
notes.3:3: "Interlude" translates Greek diapsalma, a musical pause corresponding to Hebrew selah (also in 3:9 and 3:13).
notes.3:4: The Greek reads "He established a mighty love of His strength" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "there is the hiding place of His power."
notes.3:5: The Greek vocalizes the Hebrew consonants as davar ("a word," Greek logos) rather than MT dever ("pestilence").
notes.3:19: The Greek reads "to completion" (rather than MT "like deer's feet") and translates the Hebrew musical colophon ("For the choirmaster, on my stringed instruments") as the closing clause "to triumph in His song."
